newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to tender for $1 bln pipeline for Iran gas.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to tender for $1 bln pipeline for Iran gas.

text.p: Turkey will open a tender in November to build a pipeline, estimated to cost $1 billion, for its agreed gas purchases under a recent multi-billion-dollar deal with Iran, a senior energy official said on Wednesday.
"The tender will be opened in November. The project will cost about $1 billion," said Ugur Dogan, undersecretary for the energy ministry.
"The Iranian gas agreement is going ahead as planned," he told Reuters.
The pipeline will carry an initial three billion cubic metres of Iranian natural gas annually from 1999 under a $23-billion, 23-year agreement signed between the two neighbouring countries in August.
The amount will rise to 10 billion cubic metres from 2005.

The deal requires both countries to build the pipelines in their own land in a move to avoid breaching a U.S. decision in August that non-U.S. investors putting at least $40 million in energy projects in Iran and Libya would be punished.
Officials earlier said the Iranian section of the pipeline would be about 270-km (163-mile) long from Tabriz to the Turkish border.

They said the pipeline might enter Turkey at Dogu Bayazit, and pass through Erzurum, Erzincan, Sivas and end up in Ankara, or alternately through a further southern route to feed the industrial cities of Malatya and Kayseri.
Both routes in the Turkish territory require a pipeline of about 1,150 km (720 miles) long, for which the tender will be held.
The total length of the main line will be 1,420 km (890 miles) from Tabriz to Ankara, and the whole network will be about 2,000 km (1,250 miles) including spurs, according to preliminary studies.
Dogan said a delegation of Iranian gas officials held talks with officials from Botas, Turkey's state pipeline company, in September.
Under the agreement Iran will have sold about 190 billion cubic metres of gas to Turkey.
